newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac says new spending must be matched by cuts.
newsitem.headline: Chirac says new spending must be matched by cuts.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Monday the left-wing government's plans to spend money frozen by the previous administration should be matched by savings to avoid slipping off course for monetary union.

"What I say is that 10 billion francs should be found elsewhere if we want to be among those European nations capable of taking on the single currency," Chirac said in a Bastille Day television interview. The government has said its plans to pay for new policies worth around 11 billion francs will be funded by reshuffling allocations without raising overall spending.
The Socialist-led cabinet said last week it would redirect spending plans to pay for new measures including the creation of some 40,000 to 70,000 public sector jobs for young people.

Ministers said the government would scrap or reallocate 11 billion francs ($1.9 billion) in spending planned by the previous centre-right administration and spend 11.1 billion francs on the new measures.
